messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: sustained GPU OOMs on decode/streaming pool us-west-2-streaming-01. 12 pods restarted in last 4m, 5xx spike ~20%. Thresholds: gpu_mem_pct > 90 for 3 consecutive samples. Link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/alerts/3951234567

devon: oncall responding, reading in. which model variant affected? any customer-facing 5xxs?

infra-oliver: looks like decode-runtime streaming path. logs show repeated CUDA OOM during token generation, runtime process restarts. Affected nodes: usw2-decode-nodes-3/4/7

maria: seeing increased request drops in prod routing dashboard. some customers reported partial responses then connection closed. Support has SR-1287 opening now.

devon: ok. immediate mitigations: 1) stop streaming path to reduce tail memory pressure 2) enable smaller model fallback for new requests 3) cordon and drain the worst nodes if needed. I'll coordinate.

ops-bot: action: disable-route streaming/v1 -> succeeded (api-gw:apply 200)

maria: disabling streaming reduced error rate on gateway within 30s, but decode pods still show OOM churn for existing sessions

sre-jen: joining. can we see the exact error log?

infra-oliver: paste logs from one failing pod:

```
E 10:42:11.234 decode[pid=2145] cuda error: out of memory
E 10:42:11.235 decode[pid=2145] attempt to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 24.00 GiB total)
E 10:42:11.236 decode[pid=2145] stack: at runtime/alloc.c:423
E 10:42:11.238 decode[pid=2145] FATAL: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
```

infra-oliver: also seeing repeated kworker restarts, kernel logs show page faults when allocating large KV cache slices

devon: hypothesis: runaway generation from clients hitting missing max_tokens cap. Any recent deploys to API proxy or SDK?

maria: yes — PR #1423 to api-gateway merged 6h ago. That change removed legacy header enforcement for X-Client-Max-Tokens to defer to upstream. Could be clients not sending it and runtime interpreting as unlimited.

support-ana: cross-ref with support tickets: two customers indicate unusually long completions started ~11:30 UTC, matches merge time for PR #1423.

sre-jen: switch to containment: 1) reapply global max_tokens middleware immediately 2) throttle per-session token window 3) evict oldest long-running sessions

devon: implemented middleware hotfix patch (rollback to enforce max_tokens=2048) and deployed to canary. patch id hotfix/3951

ops-bot: hotfix deploy started -> canary ok -> rolling to production (10 pods)

infra-oliver: meanwhile draining one of the noisy nodes to stop churn:

kubectl cordon usw2-decode-3
kubectl drain usw2-decode-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

maria: after block and hotfix: GPU mem pressure trending down, 5xx rate back to baseline within 3 min. Some pods still show OOMs from prior sessions but no new ones.

devon: what about requests that dropped? estimate customer impact please.

support-ana: initial tally: ~42 unique customers had at least one dropped request in the 11:28-11:40 UTC window. Escalated SR-1287 into incident. Not a full outage but degraded for streaming-heavy customers. No SLA breach at this time but will monitor.

pm-ellie: marking this Sev2 due to partial customer impact and potential data egress concerns. We need a postmortem and comms.

sre-jen: root cause hypothesis: api-gateway change removed fallback enforcement for client max_tokens, causing some SDKs (older clients) to send no cap. Decoding runtime defaults to unlimited generation in streaming path, KV cache grows, GPU OOM.

infra-oliver: supporting data: histogram of request token lengths shows a tail jump at 11:30 from median 120 -> tail 35k tokens. GPU mem per-pod correlated with long-running sessions.

devon: immediate followups (action items):
- revert PR #1423 or add strong guard in gateway to enforce max_tokens header (maria)
- add runtime guard to clip client max_tokens to safe ceiling (sre-jen)
- add continuous synthetic test generating long stream to catch runaway in CI (infra-oliver)
- add alert: per-pod consecutive OOM count > 3 -> auto-evict + scale up (devon)
- support to contact top affected customers and append credit offer if appropriate (support-ana)

maria: filed rollback PR #1435, deploying now. will include explicit header enforcement and a quick canary.

ops-bot: rollback PR #1435 merged -> rollout started -> 8/10 pods updated -> monitoring shows gateway now assigns max_tokens header 2048

sre-jen: pushing runtime clip patch: if client_max_tokens missing or > 8192 then set to min(client_max_tokens, 8192). Will also add a hard safety cap of 20k tokens for decode path. Patch id runtime/clip-395

infra-oliver: added alert rule: if streaming pod GPU mem > 88% and request token length > 10k -> fire high-priority alert with pod id and request sample.

devon: handing to SRE for follow-up. I'll update incident channel and create incident ticket INC-2026 for full postmortem.

support-ana: I opened a customer comms draft, tagging legal and account execs. Support ticket SR-1287 will get status updates and recommended next steps.

pm-ellie: please include timeline and customer impact numbers in postmortem. Also include action owner and ETA for fixes.

devon: monitoring shows error/drop rates stabilized, rolling restarts finished, no new OOM events in the last 12m. Confirming resolution window at 11:54 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Severity: 2. Incident ticket INC-2026 created. Follow-ups assigned: runtime clipping, API guard, synthetic tests, improved alerts.

devon: thanks team. I'll do the handoff to SRE for root cause and postmortem. If anyone sees regressions ping me directly. :thumbsup:

sre-jen: will drive postmortem. tentative RCA: missing max_tokens enforcement -> unbounded generation -> KV cache and GPU mem growth -> CUDA OOM -> pod restarts -> request drops.

maria: adding link to rollback diff and canary metrics: https://git.internal/redwood/api-gateway/pull/1435

support-ana: adding list of affected customers to INC-2026 and emailing AEs.

devon: closing thread.
